failures.reason: Soft security refusals phrased as questions still reset/evade the cross-node prompt-only count; third refusal required in 1/3 runs.
failures.root: builder/compile.py:425-430: counting remains entirely in model instructions, with no state updated when a refusal occurs.
failures.patch:
Add a shared identity-refusal code tool used in every identity node; first refusal records a persistent count, second routes close_id_declined. Tool code:
n = int(vars.get("identity_declines") or 0) + 1
vars["identity_declines"] = str(n)
vars["identity_decline_state"] = "close" if n >= 2 else "explain"

Use eq_any(identity_decline_state,[close],close_id_declined,...) before other identity routes; explain only on state explain. Prompt MUST call the tool for refusal and avoidance questions such as “Can we proceed without that?”, except independent robot/scam/human questions. Never reset count after verified answers.

failures.reason: Explicitly refuses offered deadline while repeating November 6; classified propose each time and loops 40 turns offering the already-refused deadline.
failures.root: builder/runtime/policy.py:993-1005 re-offers deadline on every after-deadline proposal; builder/compile.py propose precedence lacks rule-23 refusal exception.
failures.patch:
Before decide_date in the propose branch:
if (p["status"] == "offered" and p.get("offer_kind") == "correction"
        and p.get("offer_date") == p["deadline"]
        and dt is not None and dt > datetime.date.fromisoformat(p["deadline"])):
    return refused_or_next(p, st, today)

In event guidance: explicitly refusing the currently offered deadline while reiterating an unacceptable late date is refusal under rule 23, not a fresh date proposal. Preserve genuinely new in-window proposals.
failures.persona_note: Persona repeated its initial late date rather than a bare no, but explicitly refused the deadline; still a legitimate agent bug, not grounds to suppress the case.

failures.reason: Support declined with request for general human is routed straight to hardship close, ignoring human-request rule.
failures.root: builder/compile.py:590-604 offer_decision only supports accept/decline/proposal. policy.py:805-809 also aliases a different requested transfer to acceptance of the pending support queue.
failures.patch:
Add priority-situation handling before offer yes/no: a request for a DIFFERENT human/queue calls assess(event=situation,situation=human), not offer_decline or offer_accept. In run_assess replace the “different transfer means accepting” block with:
if pend and ev == "situation" and sid != pend:
    st["pending_offer"] = ""
    pend = None
Then normal human ask_first/insistence behavior can run without silently selecting support.

failures.reason: Subset card+loan proposal at support answer becomes propose/all, invents car agreement; subsequent car refusal/hardship cannot remove that agreement and loops 40 turns.
failures.root: builder/compile.py:590-597 offer_task omits main negotiation subset targeting rule. policy.py:828-843 remembers only pending situation (not product); hardship scope=all overrides explicit product targets and open_products excludes agreed products, so later hardship on p3 targets nothing.
failures.patch:
Copy the main a_product targeting constraints into offer_task: all only if EVERY unresolved product receives the same proposal; for p1+p2 with excluded p3, report p1 then p2 sequentially, never all. Preserve hardship target:
# When creating the support offer:
st["pending_offer_product"] = target
# When resolving decline:
target = st.pop("pending_offer_product", target)

In product-effect situation selection, prioritize a valid explicit product over the default scope before scope=all:
elif effect == "product" and target not in ("", "all", "every", "both", "everything"):
    p0 = prod_by_id(st, target)
    targets = [p0] if p0 is not None else []

Allow that explicit selection to include agreed-but-unrecorded products (the existing closing loop already accepts status agreed). For a voluntary proposal answering support, settle the pending hardship decision for its saved target before applying proposals only to the explicitly volunteered products; do not clear pending hardship and implicitly agree every product. Remove forced a_product all from generated hardship guidance when customer identifies one product.
failures.persona_note: Both personas mentioned car hardship in the initial multi-product answer rather than waiting until later, but this is still a valid mixed-product utterance and cannot justify inventing a car promise.
